objective: Give the model channel a measured parametric basis: propagate published k-omega SST closure-coefficient intervals through solves on the motorcycle held mesh and report the resulting drag envelope as coefficient-interval evidence alongside the current transferred estimate.

design_disclosure_one_at_a_time_vs_joint.what_was_run: 5 coefficient families (betaStar, a1, sigma-w1, betaStar/beta1, betaStar/beta2), each perturbed ONE AT A TIME: one coefficient moved to a published interval bound, every other coefficient held at its nominal SST value. This is exactly the design the agenda entry specified (its own words: 'solves one-at-a-time corner cases for the five coefficients').
design_disclosure_one_at_a_time_vs_joint.corners_run: 10 total: 1 baseline (all nominal) + 9 one-at-a-time corners (2 each for betaStar, sigma-w1, betaStar/beta1, betaStar/beta2, plus 1 for a1 since its lower bound equals its nominal value). This is ALL of the one-at-a-time corners available; none were skipped.
design_disclosure_one_at_a_time_vs_joint.corners_in_the_full_joint_box: 32 (2^5), if every coefficient's two interval bounds are treated as levels in a full factorial. Of those 32, only the 10 we ran have zero or one coefficient away from nominal; the other 22 corners move two or more coefficients at once and were NOT sampled.
design_disclosure_one_at_a_time_vs_joint.what_the_reported_band_is: A SENSITIVITY SWEEP, not the joint parametric range. It shows how far Cd moves when exactly one coefficient is pushed to a published bound, and it ranks the coefficients by that one-at-a-time swing. It is a valid, cited, measured result for that question.
design_disclosure_one_at_a_time_vs_joint.what_the_reported_band_is_not: It is NOT the full joint uncertainty range coefficient uncertainty could produce. The one-at-a-time envelope is a lower bound on the true joint range: if several coefficients can push Cd in the same direction simultaneously, as the measured signs below suggest they can, the true joint corner would move further than any single one-at-a-time sample did. This report's 'band' section below is therefore a sensitivity-sweep envelope and should be read and labelled as such, not substituted for a joint parametric band.

cheap_joint_extreme_proposal.description: Two additional runs, each moving all five coefficients at once to the bound their one-at-a-time sign favors: one corner with every coefficient set to push Cd up (betaStar=0.0784, a1=0.40, alphaOmega1=0.3, beta1 at ratio 1.19, beta2 at ratio 1.05), one corner with every coefficient set to push Cd down (betaStar=0.1024, a1=0.31 nominal since it cannot decrease, alphaOmega1=0.7, beta1 at ratio 1.31, beta2 at ratio 1.45). This is an approximate linear-superposition estimate of the joint envelope's extremes, not a rigorous joint UQ; it assumes the coefficients act close to additively, which the one-at-a-time data cannot itself confirm or rule out.
cheap_joint_extreme_proposal.estimated_cost: 2 more restart runs at the same 4-core budget. Based on this run's actual costs (1.6-1.8 core-minutes for a plateaued sample, 6.5 core-minutes for one that needed the 300-iteration extension), a conservative estimate is 4 to 16 core-minutes for the pair, well inside the 33 core-minutes remaining against the 60 core-minute stage-1 budget.
cheap_joint_extreme_proposal.status: AUTHORIZED AND RUN after the original report was written. Both corners completed and plateaued; see joint_corner_results and superposition_test in this section. The original text of this proposal is preserved above unchanged.

design_disclosure_one_at_a_time_vs_joint.corners_sampled_of_full_factorial: With 5 two-level factors the full joint factorial has 32 corners. The one-at-a-time set sampled 10 of them (zero or one coefficient away from nominal); the two joint corners bring the sampled count to 12 of 32. The other 20 corners were NOT sampled, so the joint envelope below is a linear-superposition approximation, never a rigorous joint band.

superposition_test.purpose: The two corners are a test of linear superposition, not merely a wider envelope. The prediction for each corner is the baseline Cd plus the sum of the measured one-at-a-time deltas of the coefficients being moved, computed and recorded before the corner solves were taken to plateau.

a1_low_and_high_effects_stated_separatel.a1_low_note: exactly zero BY CONSTRUCTION, not by measurement: the published Schaefer interval for a1 is [0.31, 0.40] and its lower bound coincides with the SST nominal 0.31, so the baseline run IS the a1-low sample and no separate solve exists. The local-minimum question (both a1 bounds raising Cd) cannot arise within the published interval because there is no bound below nominal; this study has no evidence about Cd for a1 below 0.31.
a1_low_and_high_effects_stated_separatel.a1_high_note: measured, a1_hi (a1=0.40) minus baseline, converged tail means

joint_up.noise_gate: the prediction error +0.004491 is compared against every oscillation scale in the chain: joint_up's own window std 0.0000402 and peak to peak 0.000175, the baseline's peak to peak 0.0019, and the largest one-at-a-time window std 0.00081. It exceeds all of them by at least a factor of 2.4 (and its own by two orders of magnitude). VERDICT: a real, resolved super-additive interaction, not limit-cycle noise.

joint_down.noise_gate: the prediction error +0.002980 is SMALLER than joint_down's own limit-cycle amplitude (half peak to peak 0.0056, window std 0.0024). At this corner superposition cannot be distinguished from limit-cycle noise at this resolution; no claim is made either way.

superposition_test.cross_check_with_stationary_window_means: Rebuilding the predictions from stationary-window means instead of the original tail-window QoIs changes nothing material: predicted joint_up 0.434668 vs measured 0.4390491 (error +0.004381), predicted joint_down 0.405904 vs measured 0.4074039 (error +0.001500). The up corner conclusion is unchanged; the down corner error remains inside its cycle amplitude.
superposition_test.conclusion: The evidence supports the interactions-matter branch. At the up corner, where every oscillation is small enough to resolve the question, the measured Cd exceeds the superposition prediction by +0.004491, which is 24.4 percent of the predicted swing and at least 2.4x every oscillation scale involved; the one-at-a-time deltas do NOT compose additively there. Both corners land ABOVE their predictions, i.e. the flow responds super-additively upward. The down corner alone is inconclusive because its limit cycle (std 0.0024) is as large as its prediction error. Consequence: the corner pair gives a linear-superposition approximation of the joint envelope, roughly 0.4074 to 0.4390 in means (width 0.0316 Cd, 7.6 percent of baseline, versus 0.0204 for the one-at-a-time band), but it must NOT be sold as a joint band, and a defensible joint band needs the stage-two LHS or Sobol design. Whether to spend those 120 core-minutes is the supervisor's call; this run only reports the measured superposition failure.
superposition_test.envelope_label: LINEAR-SUPERPOSITION APPROXIMATION ONLY. 12 of the 32 corners of the full 2^5 factorial were sampled (10 one-at-a-time plus these 2 joint corners); the true joint extremes could lie beyond either corner, and the up corner's measured super-additivity is direct evidence that additive composition misses real interaction effects.

oscillation_structure.why_this_section_exists: The joint_down corner exposed that these steady SIMPLE solves do not all settle to a fixed point: several settle onto a stationary limit cycle. An oscillating force coefficient is not automatically an unconverged solve; the operative distinction is between a solution whose mean is still moving (genuinely unconverged, any number is arbitrary) and one that has settled onto a repeating oscillation with stable mean and amplitude (converged, but the answer is a mean plus a spread, not a point). Every Cd in this study is therefore a MEAN OVER AN OSCILLATION and is reported here with its own spread.
oscillation_structure.stationary_window_rule: longest suffix of the series, stepping by 10 iterations, whose two halves have means differing by less than the suffix's own standard deviation; this accepts a stationary oscillation (halves agree within the cycle spread) and rejects drift (halves separated by more than the spread)
oscillation_structure.spread_measure_choice: Both the window standard deviation and the peak to peak excursion are reported for every sample. The std is judged the more honest routine measure because a single extreme iteration dominates peak to peak over long windows; peak to peak is included so a reader can see the full excursion a single-snapshot reading could have returned.
oscillation_structure.consistency_with_previously_reported_mea: For the ten original samples the stationary-window means differ from the previously reported tail-window cd_mean values by at most 0.00065 (largest at beta_star_hi), inside every sample's own oscillation spread. The previously reported means stand; this section adds the spread structure around them rather than revising them.

band_restated_with_oscillation_visible.statement: The 0.020401 Cd (4.90 percent) one-at-a-time band is a spread of MEANS. Each mean carries its own limit-cycle spread: peak to peak 0.0016719 to 0.0033377 Cd across the ten original samples (8 to 16 percent of the band width), 0.000175 at the joint_up corner, and 0.011223 at the joint_down corner (35 percent of the 0.0316 corner-to-corner superposition envelope). A reader taking 0.0204 Cd as the total uncertainty while a single sample can wander 0.006 Cd from its own mean within a window would overstate the precision; both numbers belong together.

oscillation_structure.physical_or_pseudo_time_view: View, offered for the parallel NACA 0012 question: the oscillation here is most plausibly physical in ORIGIN, a bluff-body wake instability of a massively separated flow at Reynolds number of order 10^6 that steady RANS renders as a limit cycle, though its amplitude and period as computed are pseudo-time artifacts and not time-accurate measurements. The evidence is that the cycle amplitude tracks modelled turbulent damping systematically: joint_up, whose coefficients (a1 0.40, betaStar 0.0784) raise eddy viscosity in the separated region, extinguishes the cycle almost completely (window std 0.0000402), while joint_down, whose coefficients lower it, shows the largest cycle in the study (std 0.0024, peak to peak 0.0112), with the nominal-coefficient samples in between (ptp about 0.002). A pure pseudo-time artifact would not be expected to respond this systematically to the turbulence closure. A bluff body at this Reynolds number is also a much stronger candidate for genuinely physical unsteadiness than an airfoil.

comparison_to_corner_envelope.corner_envelope_label: linear-superposition approximation from 2 of 32 full-factorial corners (12/32 sampled overall)
comparison_to_corner_envelope.finding: The LHS band (0.017273 Cd) is NARROWER than the two-corner envelope (0.031645 Cd), at 54.6% of its width. Per the standing rule, this is NOT read as the LHS superseding or tightening the joint estimate; it is explained by three measured, structural differences, not by interactions being unimportant:
comparison_to_corner_envelope.reason_1_fewer_factors_moved: The LHS varies only the top 3 of 5 coefficient families (a1, betaStar, betaStar/beta2 ratio); alphaOmega1 (sigma-w1) and betaStar/beta1 stay at nominal in every LHS sample, while BOTH joint corners moved all 5 to their bounds. Stage one's own OAT deltas put the combined contribution of the two omitted factors at about +0.000477 Cd toward joint_up (sigma_w1_lo +0.000391 + ratio_beta1_lo +0.0000861) and about -0.000977 Cd toward joint_down (sigma_w1_hi -0.000255 + ratio_beta1_hi -0.000722): real, but only a few percent of the 0.0143 gap between the two envelope widths.
comparison_to_corner_envelope.reason_2_maximin_lhs_avoids_vertices_by_: A maximin LHS design explicitly spreads points away from box corners (that is what min-pairwise-distance optimizes for), so no sample lands at or near the exact vertex the joint corners occupy. In the unit cube over (a1, betaStar, ratio), the nearest LHS sample to the 'all factors push Cd up' vertex (1,0,0) is s2_09 at Euclidean distance 0.258 (and it IS the LHS maximum, cd_mean=0.427305); the nearest to the 'all factors push Cd down' vertex (0,1,1) is s2_05 at distance 0.383. By design, the LHS never samples the vertex itself.
comparison_to_corner_envelope.reason_3_measured_super_additivity_at_th: Stage one's own superposition test found the joint_up corner exceeds the linear (additive) prediction by +0.0044905 Cd (24.4% of the predicted swing), resolved outside every oscillation scale involved: a real super-additive interaction at the vertex itself. Since the LHS band is built entirely from interior points and the true vertex response is measured to overshoot a smooth interior extrapolation there, the LHS envelope is expected to fall short of the corner extremum on structural grounds, independent of sample count.
comparison_to_corner_envelope.additional_observation: The LHS minimum (s2_07, cd_mean=0.410032) sits far from the 'down' vertex in unit-cube distance (0.854, not the nearest point to it) yet is the lowest of all 20 sample means; the response surface over this 3-factor box is not simply monotonic toward either vertex, corroborating rather than contradicting the interactions-matter finding from stage one.
comparison_to_corner_envelope.conclusion: Both bands are kept, not merged: the two-corner pair remains the wider, worst-case-oriented linear-superposition bound (0.4074-0.4390, 12/32 corners sampled); the 20-sample LHS band (0.4100-0.4273) is the measured, near-uniform characterization of the box INTERIOR and is the appropriate parametric basis for a distributional (not worst-case) treatment of the model channel. Neither is claimed to supersede the other.

This interior/distributional band sits inside, and must be read alongside rather than in place of, the wider 0.4074-0.4390 (0.0316 Cd, 7.6%) two-corner worst-case envelope from the 12/32 sampled full-factorial corners; the gap between them is explained above, not papered over.
